A `worktree` prevents concurrent agents from sharing one checkout; it does not\nprevent reads of sibling/user-home data, writes elsewhere, or arbitrary egress. The coordinator's\nnetwork policy is likewise advisory because it is checked only by callers that volunteer a\ndomain.\n\ndg-07 closes the local execution gap. A shared local-process backend consumes the exact dg-06\ndecision, renders the coordinator's policy for Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (SRT), and applies the\nresult to every vendor CLI lifecycle command: synchronous invocation, asynchronous submission,\npolling, and the autopilot local-provider harness.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### Immutable execution context\n\nDispatch receives a versioned execution context containing the complete dg-06 enforcement\nprojection, canonical digest of the persisted routing context, one authoritative isolation,\ncanonical worktree root, and provenance.\nThe projection includes the complete assignment (including normalized base URL), authored\nenforcement scope/write capability, and an exactly defined canonical digest document.\nThe enforcement layer never re-runs routing. Standalone review-panel calls that have no routed\ncontext resolve the already-landed dg-05 fallback once from the exact `agents.yaml` lane.\nRouted callers carry the complete context in phase payload v2; every adapter lifecycle method\naccepts that context explicitly instead of reconstructing it from cwd.\n\n### Coordinator-owned network-policy export and audit\n\n`NetworkPolicyService` gains an exact-agent export. It returns the active profile-specific and\nglobal rules, a closed default-deny contract, schema revision, and a deterministic digest.\nRendering is conservative: SRT denies take precedence, so conflicting authored rules may become\nnarrower but never wider. A malformed or unavailable cold-start export fails closed before vendor\nlaunch; only a successfully exported empty allow set is a valid deny-all policy.\n\nA narrow sandbox-execution audit endpoint durably and idempotently records applied and degraded\noutcomes. If the coordinator is unavailable, a locked mode-0600 JSONL outbox under the operator's\nXDG state directory is fsynced and retried oldest-first on later calls. An unsandboxed fallback is\nallowed only after either the coordinator event or the durable outbox record succeeds.\n\n### Pure renderer and lifecycle-owning backend\n\n`skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` provides:\n\n- pure, deterministic SRT settings rendering;\n- mode-aware filesystem policy (`review` has no project write roots; write-capable modes are\n  confined to the canonical worktree root; user-home reads are denied with narrow worktree/tool\n  and executable-install-root carve-outs; every lane gets an ephemeral vendor-state root);\n- a prepared-command lifecycle that owns a unique mode-0600 settings file, positive-allowlist child\n  environment with one lane credential,\n  runtime identity, policy digest, process group, and cleanup;\n- an additive renderer seam for future runtimes.\n\nThe reviewed runtime is `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 on Node >=20.11.0. The repository\npins the package and integrity and never installs it during dispatch. Setup/CI install the pin;\nruntime discovery is explicit absolute override, then the primary checkout resolved through the\nlinked worktree's common Git directory, then unavailable. The runtime is accepted only when\npackage metadata and integrity match. On Linux\nthe preflight also verifies `bubblewrap`, `socat`,\n`ripgrep`, user-namespace capability, architecture/seccomp support, and a real no-op SRT launch.\n\nOfficial runtime sources:\n\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47\n\n### One local command backend\n\nThe shared backend replaces direct vendor subprocess launches in `CliVendorAdapter` sync submit,\nasync submit and poll paths, fact-check/evaluation backends, quick-task, phase-fixer, and\n`autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. Poll enforcement\nfailures are collection failures retried to the existing deadline, not terminal remote-task\nfailures. A structural guard\nprevents future vendor CLI subprocess sinks outside the backend. Non-sandbox decisions preserve\nargv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior.\n\n### Loud, bounded degradation\n\nFail-open is restricted to facts known before a vendor process starts: unsupported OS, missing or\nincompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability preflight. Those cases warn, durably\naudit `applied=false`, and run the original command. Unsafe roots, malformed policy, settings\nmaterialization errors, and audit/outbox failures fail closed. Once SRT starts, a timeout or\nunknown failure never triggers an unsandboxed retry because doing so could execute work twice.\n\n## Scope Boundary\n\nThis change protects against accidental or confused local CLI behavior after sandbox startup.\nIt does not claim containment of a malicious vendor executable, a compromised runtime, same-user\nraces, damage inside an authorized writable root, or exfiltration through an allowed destination\nsuch as GitHub. It strips proxy and code-injection environment variables required to preserve the\nSRT boundary. dg-07 sandbox lanes require environment-backed authentication; file-backed login\nstate remains ineligible. Credentials deliberately supplied to a CLI remain readable by that CLI.\nRequest-time secret substitution is dg-08; broader credential brokering and cloud execution remain\nowned by `add-sandboxed-harness-execution`.\n\ndg-03's factual `posture.filesystem` means a per-session workspace exists; it is not a security\nattestation and never satisfies a router request for `sandbox`. Wrapping a local submission CLI\nalso does not imply that a remote worker is sandboxed.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Shared SRT local-process backend (selected)\n\nOne policy renderer and one lifecycle-owning runner cover every current local CLI sink. It enforces\nthe already-authored isolation and network decisions without creating a second router.\n\n### Vendor-native flags only\n\nRejected. Vendor flags differ, omit network enforcement, and leave vendors without a native\nsandbox unprotected.\n\n### Coordinator-managed containers\n\nDeferred. A container/control-plane backend belongs to the downstream sandboxed-harness change;\ndg-07 supplies the local backend and renderer seam it consumes.\n\n## Impact\n\n- New shared runtime: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` and local process backend helpers.\n- Modified execution sinks: review/fact-check/OCR dispatchers, all coordinator CLI evaluation\n  backends, quick-task/phase-fixer flows, and autopilot local-provider dispatch.\n- Modified coordinator: exact-agent policy export and durable sandbox audit endpoint.\n- Modified config projection: effective per-mode isolation reaches standalone adapters.\n- New pinned optional tool dependency: SRT 0.0.77.\n- New contracts, tests, operational documentation, and real-runtime probes.\n- New push/PR-triggered Ubuntu/macOS GitHub Actions evidence gate, with linked-worktree and pinned\n  configured-vendor executable passes bound to the exact tested SHA and verified after push.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRemoving a mode's `sandbox` decision restores the byte-compatible local process path. Removing or\nbreaking the runtime does not silently claim enforcement: the preflight records a durable degraded\nevent before the legacy command may run.\n"}]},"isError":false}

The current two subprocess call families are the multi-vendor review\ndispatcher and autopilot's local Pi provider.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Consume one immutable execution context\n\n`DispatchExecutionContext` is a normative enforcement projection of dg-06: decision id, item id,\nphase, attempt, dispatch work id, every assignment field (including nullable normalized\n`base_url`), and a canonical digest of the full persisted routing context, plus authored\n`enforcement_scope`, authored `write_capable`, and canonical root. The roadmap host constructs\nit at the dispatch boundary and passes it through `PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context`.\nPayload v2 removes the legacy top-level isolation authority; a compatibility reader rejects any\nlegacy isolation value that disagrees with the embedded context. `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()`,\n`dispatch_async()`, and `poll_for_result()` receive the same explicit context. Standalone panel\ncallers construct one context at their adapter boundary from the exact lane's mode override, then\nentry value. A router-sourced context requires router correlation and the assignment digest. No\nrenderer or backend calls routing or derives a sandbox root from ambient process cwd. Root safety\nchecks apply only while preparing `sandbox`; `none` and `worktree` preserve legacy cwd behavior.\n\nThe digest source document is exactly the validated dg-06 `RoutingDispatchContext` contract:\n`schema_version`, `decision_id`, `item_id`, `phase`, `attempt`, `dispatch_work_id`, the complete\nassignment object (including extension fields and normalized `base_url`), and optional provenance.\nMutable lifecycle fields such as status and `prepared_at` are excluded. It is SHA-256 over UTF-8\ncanonical JSON with lexicographically sorted object keys, compact separators, and no floats.\nPayload v2 carries that validated lossless routing-context object alongside the flattened\nenforcement projection. The host computes the digest immediately after dg-06 validation; the\nbackend canonicalizes the carried object, recomputes the digest, and verifies every duplicated\nflattened field against it before launch. Any float in the digest source is a typed host-side\nvalidation error. Payload-v2 `provider`, `model`, `agent_id`, and isolation duplicates are removed\nwhere compatible or must exactly equal the embedded context before any selection or launch. A\nrouter-sourced capacity fallback returns `vendor_limit` for a new router decision and\nnever silently substitutes a model. A standalone retry may create a new standalone per-attempt\ncontext.\n\nContext producers are explicit:\n\n| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy the dg-06 enforcement projection and digest into payload v2; it overrides the old phase-level `worktree` default | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |\n| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |\n| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |\n\ndg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not\ncredential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator\npolicy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.\n\n### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper\n\nAll vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in\n`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager\nvalidates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. The backend constructs argv and\nenvironment and owns process-group termination and cleanup. `build_command()` remains pure and\nvendor-specific.\n\nThe argv is `[absolute_srt, \"--settings\", settings_path, \"--\", absolute_vendor, ...]` as\ndocumented by SRT. Options that weaken nested, network, Unix-socket, local-binding, or Apple Event\nisolation are never project-configurable.\n\n### D3 — Mode-aware filesystem policy\n\nReview and validation-shaped commands receive no project write roots. Alternative, quick,\nimplementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree\nroot. `agents.yaml` authors `enforcement_scope` and `write_capable` per mode; these properties are\nnever inferred from assignment location. Autopilot maps each phase explicitly. Every sandboxed\ncommand receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root beneath a secure OS temporary parent\noutside both the user-home region and every checkout. That root is explicitly allowed for reads\nand writes and is used for HOME,\nXDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files. dg-07 sandbox lanes are eligible only when\nauthentication is environment-backed; a sandbox lane with no authored `api_key_env`, or whose\nselected key is absent, fails closed as rollout-ineligible until dg-08 can broker it safely.\nPer-lane `state_env_keys` and credential environment keys are authored in `agents.yaml`; the\nbackend points only those state keys into the ephemeral root and no renderer hard-codes a vendor.\nThe root must exist, equal `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and pass a new pure\n`is_managed_execution_root(root, common_repo)` predicate independent of environment posture. It\naccepts only registered `.git-worktrees/<change>[/<agent>]` roots and the read-only snapshot shape\ndefined in D8, and\nmust not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.\n\nThe worktree `.git` pointer and linked-worktree common Git metadata are explicitly denied for\nwrites. A sandboxed worker may edit files but skill prompts do not ask it to commit; the host\norchestrator validates and creates the save-point commit after collecting the worker result. This\navoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.\nSymlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual\nsame-user risk rather than overstated as contained.\n\nReads deny the platform user-home region (`/home` on Linux, `/Users` on macOS) and explicitly\nre-allow only the canonical worktree, read-only common Git metadata, pinned runtime/tool paths,\nthe realpath-resolved vendor executable and deterministic install root, and authored\ncredential-free inputs. Preflight proves those executable/install roots are readable before start.\nNamed credential paths and direct sibling-checkout filesystem reads remain denied. Because linked\nworktrees share a common object database, committed objects and refs belonging to sibling branches\nremain readable through the required read-only common-Git carve-out; this is an explicit residual,\nnot a claim of branch-content confidentiality.\nSystem/runtime reads outside the user-home region are a documented residual. Tests cover `git\nstatus` readability with backend-authored `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, denied Git mutation,\ncredential/sibling/arbitrary-home reads, and the\nread-only common-git carve-out.\n\n### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export\n\nThe coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.\nThe snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,\nexplicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds\n`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is\n`v1:<maximum-updated-at-UTC>:<row-count>`; an empty snapshot uses the stable sentinel\n`v1:none:0`. Migration 044 backfills `updated_at` from `created_at` and installs an update trigger.\n`policy_digest` is SHA-256 over UTF-8 canonical JSON\n(lexicographically sorted object keys, preserved rule-array order, no insignificant whitespace,\nno floats), excluding the digest field itself.\nDisabled rules are absent.\n\nOnly an enabled exact profile assignment is exportable. Unknown, disabled, or unassigned agents\nreceive a typed 404/409 response and never a global-only snapshot. Export ordering is total and\nstable: agent-profile before global, legacy priority ascending (lower number is higher priority),\ndeny before allow on ties, then\n`policy_id` ascending. Migration 044 adds constrained `destination_kind`,\n`destination_pattern`, `port`, and `updated_at` columns, parses/backfills legacy rows, and validates\nall new writes; any malformed applicable legacy row fails the whole export.\n\nSRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore\nkeeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are\nvalidated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export\nunrenderable; rules are never silently omitted. Malformed or unavailable export fails closed before\nvendor launch; it never becomes a fail-open reason or a synthetic destination list. An authored,\nsuccessfully exported empty allow set remains a valid deny-all policy. A default-allow snapshot is\nnot renderable by this backend and fails closed. The\nexport contract is authoritative for sandbox execution; the older advisory SQL matcher is not used\nto construct SRT settings. Renderer tests pin SRT 0.0.77 wildcard apex/multi-label behavior and\nprove every rendered allow is a subset of the authored effective policy. DNS names, IPv4 literals,\nand bracketed IPv6 literals are supported; CIDR belongs only to denied-resolved-address policy and\nis not accepted as a destination rule.\n\nProvider endpoints are not hard-coded in the renderer. Current seed policy lacks several vendor\nAPI domains, so dg-07 does not flip existing local lanes to `sandbox`; rollout requires an\nauthored endpoint inventory and a successful preflight. The controlled acceptance CLI exercises\nenforcement independently of production vendor endpoints.\n\nThe autopilot `local` provider is rollout-ineligible under `sandbox` until its authored hostname\nand port are exportable, its Node client is proven to use SRT's proxy path, and SRT supports the\ndestination class. Loopback, link-local, private-IP, or mDNS rejection is a fail-closed\npolicy/capability outcome, never a fail-open reason.\n\nThe renderer always supplies `deniedResolvedAddresses` for loopback, link-local, cloud metadata,\nRFC1918, CGNAT, and IPv6 ULA ranges. An explicit allow whose literal target is private is\nunrenderable and fails closed. DNS resolution into any baseline-denied range remains denied.\n\n### D5 — Sanitize boundary-shaping environment, do not claim secret brokering\n\nThe child environment is constructed from a positive allowlist rather than copied from the\ncoordinator. It contains only safe locale/terminal/time variables (`LANG`, `LC_*`, `TERM`, `TZ`),\nbackend-authored `HOME`, XDG, temporary and `PATH` variables, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, and the\nselected lane's single authored credential key. Proxy variables are set exclusively by SRT for a\nsandboxed child; the backend never injects them. Coordinator/API/database/Cloudflare variables and credentials for\nother vendors are absent. As defense in depth, the environment passed to SRT itself removes\nuppercase/lowercase `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`,\n`ALL_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY`; `NODE_OPTIONS`; `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`,\n`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`; `PYTHONPATH`, `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONSTARTUP`,\n`RUBYOPT`, `RUBYLIB`, `PERL5OPT`, `PERL5LIB`, `BASH_ENV`, and `ENV`; Git directory, worktree,\nindex, object, alternate-object, and config override variables; and `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP`.\nSRT may then author the proxy variables its child needs. This prevents an ambient parent proxy\nfrom bypassing address checks. The unsandboxed compatibility path retains the caller's original\nenvironment byte for byte. Runtime discovery records absolute Node, SRT entrypoint, `bwrap`,\n`socat`, and `rg` paths and constructs PATH from their parents, fixed root-owned non-writable\nsystem directories, and explicitly configured tool directories inside the canonical worktree;\nvendor executables are absolute and inherited descriptors are closed. Environment-backed vendor\ncredentials remain readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and the\ndownstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.\n\n### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence\n\nOnly unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe\nmay run the original command. The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,\nit appends a caller-generated stable `event_id` and fsyncs canonical JSONL under\n`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-events/outbox.jsonl`, with a 0700\nparent, 0600 file, advisory lock, and directory fsync. The state root must be absolute,\noperator-owned, no-follow/no-symlink, and outside every checkout; relative, wrong-owner,\ncheckout-contained, or symlinked roots fail closed. It is never exposed as sandbox-writable.\nFailure of both blocks dispatch. Unsafe root,\nunrenderable policy, materialization failure, and all post-SRT-start failures fail closed.\n\nEach later event attempt drains older outbox entries before writing the new one, removing a record\nonly after the endpoint acknowledges its `event_id`. Compaction holds the lock, writes a\nsame-directory 0600 temporary file, fsyncs it, atomically replaces the outbox, and fsyncs the\ndirectory. Migration 044 makes `event_id` unique; replay returns the original durable audit row id.\nThe shared `skills/shared/sandbox_audit.py` client/outbox is the frozen audit port consumed by the\nprocess backend; `skills/shared` owns both modules, `wp-policy-audit` implements the port, and\n`wp-runtime` depends on it rather than inventing a second persistence path. It uses a small stdlib\nHTTP transport compatible with the coordinator API, so it creates no dependency on coordinator\nsource or the coordination-bridge skill. Coordinator evaluation backends load the shared process\nbackend through the existing explicit `SKILLS_ROOT` file-loader pattern. Only connection failures,\ntimeouts, and 5xx responses\nmay use or retain the outbox. Authentication,\nauthorization, and schema 4xx failures on a live event fail closed. A permanently rejected queued\nrecord moves atomically to `${state_root}/dead-letter.jsonl` with mode 0600 and response metadata,\nusing the same lock, temporary-file, fsync, replace, and directory-fsync rules, then drain\ncontinues; it is never silently deleted or allowed to block all later evidence. Audit payloads\ncontain key names and digests, never prompt/argv bodies, settings bodies, or secret values. The\ndispatch-host service principal must have coordinator trust level 3 or greater for cross-agent\nexport/audit. Rejection is reported distinctly as `authorization_failed`; if the endpoint rejects\nthe event, no audit row is claimed and the vendor process does not start.\n\nOutbox resource use is bounded: each canonical record is at most 64 KiB; the active outbox is at\nmost 10,000 records or 64 MiB; one launch drains at most 100 records or five seconds with explicit\nconnect/read deadlines and a five-second lock wait. Reaching an active-outbox bound fails closed.\nDead letters rotate at 64 MiB and are retained for 30 days. Structured counters/logs report active\nrecord count/bytes, oldest age, drain failures, permanent rejections, and dead-letter count/bytes.\n\n### D7 — Pin and probe SRT\n\nThe repository pins `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity and Node\n>=20.11.0. `install.sh` and CI may run `npm ci` in the primary checkout's\n`tools/sandbox-runtime`; dispatch performs no installation. Discovery order is an explicit\nabsolute override, then the primary checkout derived from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, then\nunavailable. Linked worktrees therefore use one pinned ignored installation rather than looking\nfor their own `node_modules`; runtime copies never resolve relative to `__file__`. The backend\nlaunches the absolute Node binary and pinned absolute SRT JS entrypoint only after the package\nversion and exact package-lock resolved URL/integrity entry match installed metadata. Versions before\n0.0.16 are forbidden by the official network-escape advisory.\n\nLinux preflight checks `bwrap`, `socat`, `rg`, supported architecture/seccomp conditions,\nuser-namespace/AppArmor viability, and a no-op sandbox launch. macOS checks the Seatbelt backend,\n`sandbox-exec`, violation reporting, and a no-op launch. The current two subprocess call families are the multi-vendor review\ndispatcher and autopilot's local Pi provider.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Consume one immutable execution context\n\n`DispatchExecutionContext` is a normative enforcement projection of dg-06: decision id, item id,\nphase, attempt, dispatch work id, every assignment field (including nullable normalized\n`base_url`), and a canonical digest of the full persisted routing context, plus authored\n`enforcement_scope`, authored `write_capable`, and canonical root. The roadmap host constructs\nit at the dispatch boundary and passes it through `PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context`.\nPayload v2 removes the legacy top-level isolation authority; a compatibility reader rejects any\nlegacy isolation value that disagrees with the embedded context. `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()`,\n`dispatch_async()`, and `poll_for_result()` receive the same explicit context. Standalone panel\ncallers construct one context at their adapter boundary from the exact lane's mode override, then\nentry value. A router-sourced context requires router correlation and the assignment digest. No\nrenderer or backend calls routing or derives a sandbox root from ambient process cwd. Root safety\nchecks apply only while preparing `sandbox`; `none` and `worktree` preserve legacy cwd behavior.\n\nThe digest source document is exactly the validated dg-06 `RoutingDispatchContext` contract:\n`schema_version`, `decision_id`, `item_id`, `phase`, `attempt`, `dispatch_work_id`, the complete\nassignment object (including extension fields and normalized `base_url`), and optional provenance.\nMutable lifecycle fields such as status and `prepared_at` are excluded. It is SHA-256 over UTF-8\ncanonical JSON with lexicographically sorted object keys, compact separators, and no floats.\nPayload v2 carries that validated lossless routing-context object alongside the flattened\nenforcement projection. The host computes the digest immediately after dg-06 validation; the\nbackend canonicalizes the carried object, recomputes the digest, and verifies every duplicated\nflattened field against it before launch. Any float in the digest source is a typed host-side\nvalidation error. Payload-v2 `provider`, `model`, `agent_id`, and isolation duplicates are removed\nwhere compatible or must exactly equal the embedded context before any selection or launch. A\nrouter-sourced capacity fallback returns `vendor_limit` for a new router decision and\nnever silently substitutes a model. A standalone retry may create a new standalone per-attempt\ncontext.\n\nContext producers are explicit:\n\n| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy the dg-06 enforcement projection and digest into payload v2; it overrides the old phase-level `worktree` default | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |\n| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |\n| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |\n\ndg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not\ncredential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator\npolicy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.\n\n### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper\n\nAll vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in\n`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager\nvalidates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. The backend constructs argv and\nenvironment and owns process-group termination and cleanup. `build_command()` remains pure and\nvendor-specific.\n\nThe argv is `[absolute_srt, \"--settings\", settings_path, \"--\", absolute_vendor, ...]` as\ndocumented by SRT. Options that weaken nested, network, Unix-socket, local-binding, or Apple Event\nisolation are never project-configurable.\n\n### D3 — Mode-aware filesystem policy\n\nReview and validation-shaped commands receive no project write roots. Alternative, quick,\nimplementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree\nroot. `agents.yaml` authors `enforcement_scope` and `write_capable` per mode; these properties are\nnever inferred from assignment location. Autopilot maps each phase explicitly. Every sandboxed\ncommand receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root beneath a secure OS temporary parent\noutside both the user-home region and every checkout. That root is explicitly allowed for reads\nand writes and is used for HOME,\nXDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files. dg-07 sandbox lanes are eligible only when\nauthentication is environment-backed; a sandbox lane with no authored `api_key_env`, or whose\nselected key is absent, fails closed as rollout-ineligible until dg-08 can broker it safely.\nPer-lane `state_env_keys` and credential environment keys are authored in `agents.yaml`; the\nbackend points only those state keys into the ephemeral root and no renderer hard-codes a vendor.\nThe root must exist, equal `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and pass a new pure\n`is_managed_execution_root(root, common_repo)` predicate independent of environment posture. It\naccepts only registered `.git-worktrees/<change>[/<agent>]` roots and the read-only snapshot shape\ndefined in D8, and\nmust not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.\n\nThe worktree `.git` pointer and linked-worktree common Git metadata are explicitly denied for\nwrites. A sandboxed worker may edit files but skill prompts do not ask it to commit; the host\norchestrator validates and creates the save-point commit after collecting the worker result. This\navoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.\nSymlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual\nsame-user risk rather than overstated as contained.\n\nReads deny the platform user-home region (`/home` on Linux, `/Users` on macOS) and explicitly\nre-allow only the canonical worktree, read-only common Git metadata, pinned runtime/tool paths,\nthe realpath-resolved vendor executable and deterministic install root, and authored\ncredential-free inputs. Preflight proves those executable/install roots are readable before start.\nNamed credential paths and direct sibling-checkout filesystem reads remain denied. Because linked\nworktrees share a common object database, committed objects and refs belonging to sibling branches\nremain readable through the required read-only common-Git carve-out; this is an explicit residual,\nnot a claim of branch-content confidentiality.\nSystem/runtime reads outside the user-home region are a documented residual. Tests cover `git\nstatus` readability with backend-authored `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, denied Git mutation,\ncredential/sibling/arbitrary-home reads, and the\nread-only common-git carve-out.\n\n### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export\n\nThe coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.\nThe snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,\nexplicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds\n`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is\n`v1:<maximum-updated-at-UTC>:<row-count>`; an empty snapshot uses the stable sentinel\n`v1:none:0`. Migration 044 backfills `updated_at` from `created_at` and installs an update trigger.\n`policy_digest` is SHA-256 over UTF-8 canonical JSON\n(lexicographically sorted object keys, preserved rule-array order, no insignificant whitespace,\nno floats), excluding the digest field itself.\nDisabled rules are absent.\n\nOnly an enabled exact profile assignment is exportable. Unknown, disabled, or unassigned agents\nreceive a typed 404/409 response and never a global-only snapshot. Export ordering is total and\nstable: agent-profile before global, legacy priority ascending (lower number is higher priority),\ndeny before allow on ties, then\n`policy_id` ascending. Migration 044 adds constrained `destination_kind`,\n`destination_pattern`, `port`, and `updated_at` columns, parses/backfills legacy rows, and validates\nall new writes; any malformed applicable legacy row fails the whole export.\n\nSRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore\nkeeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are\nvalidated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export\nunrenderable; rules are never silently omitted. Malformed or unavailable export fails closed before\nvendor launch; it never becomes a fail-open reason or a synthetic destination list. An authored,\nsuccessfully exported empty allow set remains a valid deny-all policy. A default-allow snapshot is\nnot renderable by this backend and fails closed. The\nexport contract is authoritative for sandbox execution; the older advisory SQL matcher is not used\nto construct SRT settings. Renderer tests pin SRT 0.0.77 wildcard apex/multi-label behavior and\nprove every rendered allow is a subset of the authored effective policy. DNS names, IPv4 literals,\nand bracketed IPv6 literals are supported; CIDR belongs only to denied-resolved-address policy and\nis not accepted as a destination rule.\n\nProvider endpoints are not hard-coded in the renderer. Current seed policy lacks several vendor\nAPI domains, so dg-07 does not flip existing local lanes to `sandbox`; rollout requires an\nauthored endpoint inventory and a successful preflight. The controlled acceptance CLI exercises\nenforcement independently of production vendor endpoints.\n\nThe autopilot `local` provider is rollout-ineligible under `sandbox` until its authored hostname\nand port are exportable, its Node client is proven to use SRT's proxy path, and SRT supports the\ndestination class. Loopback, link-local, private-IP, or mDNS rejection is a fail-closed\npolicy/capability outcome, never a fail-open reason.\n\nThe renderer always supplies `deniedResolvedAddresses` for loopback, link-local, cloud metadata,\nRFC1918, CGNAT, and IPv6 ULA ranges. An explicit allow whose literal target is private is\nunrenderable and fails closed. DNS resolution into any baseline-denied range remains denied.\n\n### D5 — Sanitize boundary-shaping environment, do not claim secret brokering\n\nThe child environment is constructed from a positive allowlist rather than copied from the\ncoordinator. It contains only safe locale/terminal/time variables (`LANG`, `LC_*`, `TERM`, `TZ`),\nbackend-authored `HOME`, XDG, temporary and `PATH` variables, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, and the\nselected lane's single authored credential key. Proxy variables are set exclusively by SRT for a\nsandboxed child; the backend never injects them. Coordinator/API/database/Cloudflare variables and credentials for\nother vendors are absent. As defense in depth, the environment passed to SRT itself removes\nuppercase/lowercase `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`,\n`ALL_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY`; `NODE_OPTIONS`; `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`,\n`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`; `PYTHONPATH`, `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONSTARTUP`,\n`RUBYOPT`, `RUBYLIB`, `PERL5OPT`, `PERL5LIB`, `BASH_ENV`, and `ENV`; Git directory, worktree,\nindex, object, alternate-object, and config override variables; and `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP`.\nSRT may then author the proxy variables its child needs. This prevents an ambient parent proxy\nfrom bypassing address checks. The unsandboxed compatibility path retains the caller's original\nenvironment byte for byte. Runtime discovery records absolute Node, SRT entrypoint, `bwrap`,\n`socat`, and `rg` paths and constructs PATH from their parents, fixed root-owned non-writable\nsystem directories, and explicitly configured tool directories inside the canonical worktree;\nvendor executables are absolute and inherited descriptors are closed. Environment-backed vendor\ncredentials remain readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and the\ndownstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.\n\n### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence\n\nOnly unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe\nmay run the original command. The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,\nit appends a caller-generated stable `event_id` and fsyncs canonical JSONL under\n`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-events/outbox.jsonl`, with a 0700\nparent, 0600 file, advisory lock, and directory fsync. The state root must be absolute,\noperator-owned, no-follow/no-symlink, and outside every checkout; relative, wrong-owner,\ncheckout-contained, or symlinked roots fail closed. It is never exposed as sandbox-writable.\nFailure of both blocks dispatch. Unsafe root,\nunrenderable policy, materialization failure, and all post-SRT-start failures fail closed.\n\nEach later event attempt drains older outbox entries before writing the new one, removing a record\nonly after the endpoint acknowledges its `event_id`. Compaction holds the lock, writes a\nsame-directory 0600 temporary file, fsyncs it, atomically replaces the outbox, and fsyncs the\ndirectory. Migration 044 makes `event_id` unique; replay returns the original durable audit row id.\nThe shared `skills/shared/sandbox_audit.py` client/outbox is the frozen audit port consumed by the\nprocess backend; `skills/shared` owns both modules, `wp-policy-audit` implements the port, and\n`wp-runtime` depends on it rather than inventing a second persistence path. It uses a small stdlib\nHTTP transport compatible with the coordinator API, so it creates no dependency on coordinator\nsource or the coordination-bridge skill. Coordinator evaluation backends load the shared process\nbackend through the existing explicit `SKILLS_ROOT` file-loader pattern. Only connection failures,\ntimeouts, and 5xx responses\nmay use or retain the outbox. Authentication,\nauthorization, and schema 4xx failures on a live event fail closed. A permanently rejected queued\nrecord moves atomically to `${state_root}/dead-letter.jsonl` with mode 0600 and response metadata,\nusing the same lock, temporary-file, fsync, replace, and directory-fsync rules, then drain\ncontinues; it is never silently deleted or allowed to block all later evidence. Audit payloads\ncontain key names and digests, never prompt/argv bodies, settings bodies, or secret values. The\ndispatch-host service principal must have coordinator trust level 3 or greater for cross-agent\nexport/audit. Rejection is reported distinctly as `authorization_failed`; if the endpoint rejects\nthe event, no audit row is claimed and the vendor process does not start.\n\nOutbox resource use is bounded: each canonical record is at most 64 KiB; the active outbox is at\nmost 10,000 records or 64 MiB; one launch drains at most 100 records or five seconds with explicit\nconnect/read deadlines and a five-second lock wait. Reaching an active-outbox bound fails closed.\nDead letters rotate at 64 MiB and are retained for 30 days. Structured counters/logs report active\nrecord count/bytes, oldest age, drain failures, permanent rejections, and dead-letter count/bytes.\n\n### D7 — Pin and probe SRT\n\nThe repository pins `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity and Node\n>=20.11.0. `install.sh` and CI may run `npm ci` in the primary checkout's\n`tools/sandbox-runtime`; dispatch performs no installation. Exporting another agent's policy requires\ntrust level 3 or greater so the dispatch host can prepare a child without granting arbitrary agents\ncross-agent policy discovery.\nThe exact agent SHALL have an enabled profile assignment; unknown, disabled, or unassigned agents\nSHALL return a typed 404/409 and SHALL NOT receive a global-only export. Ordering SHALL be total:\nprofile before global, priority ascending (preserving legacy lower-is-higher semantics), deny before\nallow on ties, then policy id ascending.\nThe empty revision SHALL be `v1:none:0`.\n\n#### Scenario: Exact-agent export preserves authored rules\n\nWHEN an agent has profile-specific and global network rules\nTHEN export SHALL include only that profile's enabled rules and enabled global rules\nAND profile-specific precedence and authored priority SHALL be explicit.\n\n#### Scenario: Rendering never widens policy\n\nWHEN authored precedence cannot be represented exactly by SRT deny-first semantics\nTHEN the exported rules SHALL render to a conservative narrower result\nAND no destination absent from the authored effective policy SHALL be introduced.\n\n#### Scenario: Policy outage denies network\n\nWHEN an exact-agent export is unavailable or malformed at cold start\nTHEN sandbox preparation SHALL fail closed before vendor process start\nAND SHALL NOT synthesize a destination list or treat the outage as fail-open.\n\n### Requirement: Sandbox execution events SHALL be durably auditable\n\nThe coordinator SHALL accept a narrow sandbox execution event and SHALL not acknowledge durable\nsuccess until the audit row is inserted. `event_id` SHALL be generated once by the caller, remain\nstable through outbox replay, and be an idempotency key; replay SHALL return the original audit row\nid and `replayed=true`. Events SHALL include routing correlation and full-context digest, execution\nlocation and authored scope/write capability, requested and applied isolation, runtime/preflight\noutcome, policy revision/digest and endpoint digest (never raw endpoint credentials), canonical\nroot, executable paths, allowed environment key names, and degradation reason without secret\nvalues.\n\nThe server SHALL author `created_at`. `sandbox_applied=true` SHALL require the SRT backend,\nsuccessful preflight, non-null runtime/policy/settings/root evidence, and no degradation reason.\n`sandbox_applied=false` SHALL require a degradation reason. Cleanup failure SHALL carry residual\nowned paths.\n\nThe request's `agent_id` names the target CLI lane; the audit actor SHALL be derived from the\nauthenticated principal and SHALL NOT be accepted from request JSON. Recording an event for\nanother agent requires trust level 3 or greater.\n\n#### Scenario: Durable degradation event precedes fallback\n\nWHEN sandbox preflight permits an unsandboxed fallback\nTHEN the coordinator SHALL persist `applied=false` before acknowledging the event\nAND the fallback process SHALL not start before acknowledgement or a durable local outbox write.\n\n#### Scenario: Permanent outbox rejection does not poison later evidence\n\nWHEN an older queued event receives a permanent 4xx response during drain\nTHEN that record SHALL move atomically to a durable dead-letter file with response metadata\nAND later queued records MAY continue draining\nAND a live event receiving 4xx SHALL fail closed rather than enter the outbox.\n\n#### Scenario: Secret values are excluded\n\nWHEN a sandbox execution event is persisted\nTHEN environment metadata SHALL contain key names only\nAND argv prompt bodies, credential values, and settings-file contents SHALL be absent.\n"}]},"isError":false}

This\nincludes synchronous execution, asynchronous submission/polling, fact-check CLIs, coordinator\nevaluation backends, quick-task, phase-fixer mutations, and the autopilot local-provider harness.\nDiscovery and health probes are control-plane operations and are explicitly excluded. A maintained\nproduction-surface registry SHALL make new local CLI surfaces fail configuration/structural tests\nuntil classified. No cancellation subprocess exists today; any future configured vendor\ncancellation command SHALL use the same backend.\n\n#### Scenario: Every vendor lifecycle command uses the backend\n\nWHEN a configured local vendor CLI is submitted, polled, or run synchronously\nTHEN exactly one shared backend invocation SHALL own process creation\nAND a structural guard SHALL reject new direct vendor subprocess sinks.\n\n#### Scenario: Non-sandbox behavior remains compatible\n\nWHEN effective isolation is `none` or `worktree`\nTHEN the backend SHALL preserve argv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior\nAND no sandbox settings file SHALL be created.\n\n### Requirement: Enforcement SHALL consume the immutable routing decision\n\nThe backend SHALL consume the dg-06 enforcement projection and canonical full-context digest\nattached to dispatch context and SHALL NOT call routing again. Payload v2 SHALL have one isolation\nauthority: the embedded context. A standalone caller without routed context SHALL resolve dg-05's\nexact-lane fallback once at the adapter boundary and record that provenance.\nThe canonical digest source SHALL be the complete dg-06 routing contract, including every\nassignment extension and nullable normalized base URL, but excluding mutable lifecycle state.\nPayload v2 SHALL carry that lossless source and SHALL reject any mismatch between its flattened\nprojection and duplicated provider/model/agent/isolation fields before selection or launch.\nRouter-sourced capacity fallback SHALL request a new routing decision rather than substitute a\nmodel locally.\n\n#### Scenario: Routed execution is not re-resolved\n\nWHEN dispatch context carries a validated routing decision and isolation assignment\nTHEN the same decision identifier, enforcement projection, and full-context digest SHALL appear in\nthe execution audit\nAND no router request SHALL occur during rendering, preparation, or process execution.\n\n#### Scenario: Standalone dispatch resolves the exact lane\n\nWHEN a review-panel dispatch has no routed context\nTHEN effective isolation SHALL be resolved from its exact agent id and dispatch mode\nAND an entry-level value SHALL be inherited only when that mode has no override.\n\n### Requirement: Sandbox rendering SHALL be pure and mode-aware\n\nThe SRT renderer SHALL be deterministic and side-effect free. Review mode SHALL receive no project\nworktree write access. Each mode SHALL explicitly author enforcement scope and write capability;\nthese SHALL NOT be inferred from assignment location. Write-capable modes MAY write only beneath a\nstrictly resolved canonical Git worktree root. Per-launch vendor state SHALL be isolated from the operator's home. The user-home\nregion SHALL be read-denied with narrow read-only worktree/common-Git/tool carve-outs. Credential\nfiles and sibling checkout reads SHALL remain denied; dg-07 sandbox rollout requires\nenvironment-backed authentication pending dg-08.\n\n#### Scenario: Review is read-only\n\nWHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for review\nTHEN `filesystem.allowWrite` SHALL contain no project path\nAND an attempted project write SHALL leave no persistent host mutation\nAND only the backend-owned ephemeral state root and SRT's documented internal paths MAY remain\nwritable.\n\n#### Scenario: Write-capable work is root-confined\n\nWHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for an alternative or quick dispatch\nTHEN the only project write root SHALL be the canonical worktree root\nAND the worktree `.git` pointer and common Git metadata SHALL be denied for writes\nAND writes through path or symlink escapes SHALL fail.\n\n#### Scenario: User-home reads are confined\n\nWHEN a sandboxed vendor process reads the canonical worktree and linked-worktree Git metadata\nTHEN those reads SHALL succeed\nAND reads of a credential fixture, sibling checkout, or unrelated user-home file SHALL fail.\n\n#### Scenario: Rendering has no effects\n\nWHEN identical validated context and policy inputs are rendered twice\nTHEN the policy documents and digests SHALL be identical\nAND rendering SHALL NOT write files, spawn processes, or contact a service.\n\n### Requirement: Prepared sandbox commands SHALL own lifecycle and truthful state\n\nThe impure preparation layer SHALL own a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized child\nenvironment, absolute executable paths, process group, applied/degraded metadata, and cleanup.\nThe wrapped argv SHALL separate SRT options from the vendor argv with `--`.\nThe child environment SHALL be built from a positive safe baseline plus backend-authored state,\npath/proxy variables and exactly the selected lane credential; unrelated parent secrets SHALL not\nbe inherited. The renderer SHALL deny private, loopback, link-local, metadata, CGNAT, and ULA\nresolved addresses even when a hostname resolves to them.\nThe backend SHALL inject `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`; it SHALL not inherit that variable from the parent.\n\n#### Scenario: Concurrent launches do not share policy material\n\nWHEN two sandboxed commands are prepared concurrently\nTHEN each SHALL receive a distinct settings path\nAND success, failure, and timeout SHALL remove only that command's material.\n\n#### Scenario: Timeout terminates the complete process tree\n\nWHEN a sandboxed vendor command exceeds its timeout\nTHEN the backend SHALL terminate its process group, wait, escalate if required, and clean up\nAND no child process, listener, settings file, or owned mount artifact SHALL remain.\n\n#### Scenario: Execution metadata is truthful\n\nWHEN a sandbox was requested but not applied\nTHEN result and audit metadata SHALL report `requested=sandbox` and `applied=false`\nAND the dispatch SHALL NOT describe itself as sandboxed.\n\n#### Scenario: Legacy payload cannot claim sandbox enforcement\n\nWHEN a payload-v1 caller requests `sandbox`\nTHEN dispatch SHALL fail closed with `upgrade_required`\nAND only payload v2 with an embedded validated context MAY proceed.\n\n### Requirement: Degradation SHALL be narrow, durable, and pre-launch\n\nSandbox execution events SHALL be emitted only for requested `sandbox` isolation. Unsandboxed\nfallback SHALL occur only for a preflight-proven unsupported platform, absent or\nincompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability probe. A warning and durable audit or\noutbox event SHALL exist before launch. Unsafe roots, malformed policies, and audit persistence\nfailure SHALL fail closed. Malformed or unavailable policy SHALL fail before process start; an\nauthored valid empty-allow policy remains a usable deny-all sandbox. No post-launch sandbox\nfailure SHALL be retried unsandboxed.\n\n#### Scenario: Missing runtime degrades visibly\n\nWHEN isolation is `sandbox` and the pinned runtime is absent\nTHEN a durable `applied=false` event SHALL be recorded before the original command starts\nAND the command MAY proceed unsandboxed with a warning.\n\n#### Scenario: Audit failure blocks fail-open\n\nWHEN neither coordinator audit persistence nor the local durable outbox succeeds\nTHEN the unsandboxed vendor command SHALL NOT start.\n\n#### Scenario: Poll enforcement failure does not abandon remote work\n\nWHEN an asynchronous poll is blocked before its vendor process starts by sandbox enforcement\nTHEN the collector SHALL retain the remote task and retry until its existing deadline\nAND SHALL NOT classify the remote vendor task itself as failed\nAND deadline exhaustion SHALL record `remote_state_unknown`, not terminal vendor failure.\n\n#### Scenario: Runtime failure never duplicates work\n\nWHEN SRT has started and exits nonzero or times out\nTHEN the backend SHALL return that failure\nAND SHALL NOT retry the vendor command without the sandbox.\n\n### Requirement: The runtime dependency SHALL be pinned and probed\n\nThe supported SRT package version and integrity SHALL be committed. Dispatch SHALL never install a\nruntime. Runtime selection SHALL validate package metadata, Node's version floor, platform\ndependencies, and a no-op launch before reporting `applied=true`.\n\n#### Scenario: Incompatible runtime is not trusted\n\nWHEN an executable named `srt` is present but its package metadata does not match the pin\nTHEN the preflight SHALL classify it as incompatible\nAND degradation SHALL follow the durable pre-launch path.\n\n#### Scenario: Known network-escape versions are rejected\n\nWHEN the detected package version is older than 0.0.16\nTHEN it SHALL never be used for network enforcement.\n"}]},"isError":false}

Add Dispatch Sandbox Enforcement\n\n> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance` (`dg-07`)\n> Change ID: `add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement`\n> Prerequisites: dg-02, dg-03, dg-05, and dg-06 are landed\n\n## Why\n\nThe router now chooses an isolation posture and the orchestrator carries that immutable\ndecision to execution, but local vendor CLI processes still run with the host user's OS\nauthority. A `worktree` prevents concurrent agents from sharing one checkout; it does not\nprevent reads of sibling/user-home data, writes elsewhere, or arbitrary egress. The coordinator's\nnetwork policy is likewise advisory because it is checked only by callers that volunteer a\ndomain.\n\ndg-07 closes the local execution gap. A shared local-process backend consumes the exact dg-06\ndecision, renders the coordinator's policy for Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (SRT), and applies the\nresult to every vendor CLI lifecycle command: synchronous invocation, asynchronous submission,\npolling, and the autopilot local-provider harness.\n\n## What Changes\n\n### Immutable execution context\n\nDispatch receives a versioned execution context containing the complete dg-06 enforcement\nprojection, canonical digest of the persisted routing context, one authoritative isolation,\ncanonical worktree root, and provenance.\nThe projection includes the complete assignment (including normalized base URL), authored\nenforcement scope/write capability, and an exactly defined canonical digest document.\nThe enforcement layer never re-runs routing. Standalone review-panel calls that have no routed\ncontext resolve the already-landed dg-05 fallback once from the exact `agents.yaml` lane.\nRouted callers carry the complete context in phase payload v2; every adapter lifecycle method\naccepts that context explicitly instead of reconstructing it from cwd.\n\n### Coordinator-owned network-policy export and audit\n\n`NetworkPolicyService` gains an exact-agent export. It returns the active profile-specific and\nglobal rules, a closed default-deny contract, schema revision, and a deterministic digest.\nRendering is conservative: SRT denies take precedence, so conflicting authored rules may become\nnarrower but never wider. A malformed or unavailable cold-start export fails closed before vendor\nlaunch; only a successfully exported empty allow set is a valid deny-all policy.\n\nA narrow sandbox-execution audit endpoint durably and idempotently records applied and degraded\noutcomes. If the coordinator is unavailable, a locked mode-0600 JSONL outbox under the operator's\nXDG state directory is fsynced and retried oldest-first on later calls. An unsandboxed fallback is\nallowed only after either the coordinator event or the durable outbox record succeeds.\n\n### Pure renderer and lifecycle-owning backend\n\n`skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` provides:\n\n- pure, deterministic SRT settings rendering;\n- mode-aware filesystem policy (`review` has no project write roots; write-capable modes are\n  confined to the canonical worktree root; user-home reads are denied with narrow worktree/tool\n  and executable-install-root carve-outs; every lane gets an ephemeral vendor-state root);\n- a prepared-command lifecycle that owns a unique mode-0600 settings file, positive-allowlist child\n  environment with one lane credential,\n  runtime identity, policy digest, process group, and cleanup;\n- an additive renderer seam for future runtimes.\n\nThe reviewed runtime is `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 on Node >=20.11.0. The repository\npins the package and integrity and never installs it during dispatch. Setup/CI install the pin;\nruntime discovery is explicit absolute override, then the primary checkout resolved through the\nlinked worktree's common Git directory, then unavailable. The runtime is accepted only when\npackage metadata and integrity match. On Linux\nthe preflight also verifies `bubblewrap`, `socat`,\n`ripgrep`, user-namespace capability, architecture/seccomp support, and a real no-op SRT launch.\n\nOfficial runtime sources:\n\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json\n- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47\n\n### One local command backend\n\nThe shared backend replaces direct vendor subprocess launches in `CliVendorAdapter` sync submit,\nasync submit and poll paths, fact-check/evaluation backends, quick-task, phase-fixer, and\n`autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. Poll enforcement\nfailures are collection failures retried to the existing deadline, not terminal remote-task\nfailures. A structural guard\nprevents future vendor CLI subprocess sinks outside the backend. Non-sandbox decisions preserve\nargv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior.\n\n### Loud, bounded degradation\n\nFail-open is restricted to facts known before a vendor process starts: unsupported OS, missing or\nincompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability preflight. Those cases warn, durably\naudit `applied=false`, and run the original command. Unsafe roots, malformed policy, settings\nmaterialization errors, and audit/outbox failures fail closed. Once SRT starts, a timeout or\nunknown failure never triggers an unsandboxed retry because doing so could execute work twice.\n\n## Scope Boundary\n\nThis change protects against accidental or confused local CLI behavior after sandbox startup.\nIt does not claim containment of a malicious vendor executable, a compromised runtime, same-user\nraces, damage inside an authorized writable root, or exfiltration through an allowed destination\nsuch as GitHub. It strips proxy and code-injection environment variables required to preserve the\nSRT boundary. dg-07 sandbox lanes require environment-backed authentication; file-backed login\nstate remains ineligible. Credentials deliberately supplied to a CLI remain readable by that CLI.\nRequest-time secret substitution is dg-08; broader credential brokering and cloud execution remain\nowned by `add-sandboxed-harness-execution`.\n\ndg-03's factual `posture.filesystem` means a per-session workspace exists; it is not a security\nattestation and never satisfies a router request for `sandbox`. Wrapping a local submission CLI\nalso does not imply that a remote worker is sandboxed.\n\n## Approaches Considered\n\n### Shared SRT local-process backend (selected)\n\nOne policy renderer and one lifecycle-owning runner cover every current local CLI sink. It enforces\nthe already-authored isolation and network decisions without creating a second router.\n\n### Vendor-native flags only\n\nRejected. Vendor flags differ, omit network enforcement, and leave vendors without a native\nsandbox unprotected.\n\n### Coordinator-managed containers\n\nDeferred. A container/control-plane backend belongs to the downstream sandboxed-harness change;\ndg-07 supplies the local backend and renderer seam it consumes.\n\n## Impact\n\n- New shared runtime: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` and local process backend helpers.\n- Modified execution sinks: review/fact-check/OCR dispatchers, all coordinator CLI evaluation\n  backends, quick-task/phase-fixer flows, and autopilot local-provider dispatch.\n- Modified coordinator: exact-agent policy export and durable sandbox audit endpoint.\n- Modified config projection: effective per-mode isolation reaches standalone adapters.\n- New pinned optional tool dependency: SRT 0.0.77.\n- New contracts, tests, operational documentation, and real-runtime probes.\n- New push/PR-triggered Ubuntu/macOS GitHub Actions evidence gate, with linked-worktree and pinned\n  configured-vendor executable passes bound to the exact tested SHA and verified after push.\n\n## Rollback\n\nRemoving a mode's `sandbox` decision restores the byte-compatible local process path. The current two subprocess call families are the multi-vendor review\ndispatcher and autopilot's local Pi provider.\n\n## Decisions\n\n### D1 — Consume one immutable execution context\n\n`DispatchExecutionContext` is a normative enforcement projection of dg-06: decision id, item id,\nphase, attempt, dispatch work id, every assignment field (including nullable normalized\n`base_url`), and a canonical digest of the full persisted routing context, plus authored\n`enforcement_scope`, authored `write_capable`, and canonical root. The roadmap host constructs\nit at the dispatch boundary and passes it through `PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context`.\nPayload v2 removes the legacy top-level isolation authority; a compatibility reader rejects any\nlegacy isolation value that disagrees with the embedded context. `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()`,\n`dispatch_async()`, and `poll_for_result()` receive the same explicit context. Standalone panel\ncallers construct one context at their adapter boundary from the exact lane's mode override, then\nentry value. A router-sourced context requires router correlation and the assignment digest. No\nrenderer or backend calls routing or derives a sandbox root from ambient process cwd. Root safety\nchecks apply only while preparing `sandbox`; `none` and `worktree` preserve legacy cwd behavior.\n\nThe digest source document is exactly the validated dg-06 `RoutingDispatchContext` contract:\n`schema_version`, `decision_id`, `item_id`, `phase`, `attempt`, `dispatch_work_id`, the complete\nassignment object (including extension fields and normalized `base_url`), and optional provenance.\nMutable lifecycle fields such as status and `prepared_at` are excluded. It is SHA-256 over UTF-8\ncanonical JSON with lexicographically sorted object keys, compact separators, and no floats.\nPayload v2 carries that validated lossless routing-context object alongside the flattened\nenforcement projection. The host computes the digest immediately after dg-06 validation; the\nbackend canonicalizes the carried object, recomputes the digest, and verifies every duplicated\nflattened field against it before launch. Any float in the digest source is a typed host-side\nvalidation error. Payload-v2 `provider`, `model`, `agent_id`, and isolation duplicates are removed\nwhere compatible or must exactly equal the embedded context before any selection or launch. A\nrouter-sourced capacity fallback returns `vendor_limit` for a new router decision and\nnever silently substitutes a model. A standalone retry may create a new standalone per-attempt\ncontext.\n\nContext producers are explicit:\n\n| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy the dg-06 enforcement projection and digest into payload v2; it overrides the old phase-level `worktree` default | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |\n| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |\n| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |\n\ndg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not\ncredential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator\npolicy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.\n\n### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper\n\nAll vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in\n`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager\nvalidates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. The backend constructs argv and\nenvironment and owns process-group termination and cleanup. `build_command()` remains pure and\nvendor-specific.\n\nThe argv is `[absolute_srt, \"--settings\", settings_path, \"--\", absolute_vendor, ...]` as\ndocumented by SRT. Options that weaken nested, network, Unix-socket, local-binding, or Apple Event\nisolation are never project-configurable.\n\n### D3 — Mode-aware filesystem policy\n\nReview and validation-shaped commands receive no project write roots. Alternative, quick,\nimplementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree\nroot. `agents.yaml` authors `enforcement_scope` and `write_capable` per mode; these properties are\nnever inferred from assignment location. Autopilot maps each phase explicitly. Every sandboxed\ncommand receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root beneath a secure OS temporary parent\noutside both the user-home region and every checkout. That root is explicitly allowed for reads\nand writes and is used for HOME,\nXDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files. dg-07 sandbox lanes are eligible only when\nauthentication is environment-backed; a sandbox lane with no authored `api_key_env`, or whose\nselected key is absent, fails closed as rollout-ineligible until dg-08 can broker it safely.\nPer-lane `state_env_keys` and credential environment keys are authored in `agents.yaml`; the\nbackend points only those state keys into the ephemeral root and no renderer hard-codes a vendor.\nThe root must exist, equal `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and pass a new pure\n`is_managed_execution_root(root, common_repo)` predicate independent of environment posture. It\naccepts only registered `.git-worktrees/<change>[/<agent>]` roots and the read-only snapshot shape\ndefined in D8, and\nmust not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.\n\nThe worktree `.git` pointer and linked-worktree common Git metadata are explicitly denied for\nwrites. A sandboxed worker may edit files but skill prompts do not ask it to commit; the host\norchestrator validates and creates the save-point commit after collecting the worker result. This\navoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.\nSymlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual\nsame-user risk rather than overstated as contained.\n\nReads deny the platform user-home region (`/home` on Linux, `/Users` on macOS) and explicitly\nre-allow only the canonical worktree, read-only common Git metadata, pinned runtime/tool paths,\nthe realpath-resolved vendor executable and deterministic install root, and authored\ncredential-free inputs. Preflight proves those executable/install roots are readable before start.\nNamed credential paths and direct sibling-checkout filesystem reads remain denied. Because linked\nworktrees share a common object database, committed objects and refs belonging to sibling branches\nremain readable through the required read-only common-Git carve-out; this is an explicit residual,\nnot a claim of branch-content confidentiality.\nSystem/runtime reads outside the user-home region are a documented residual. Tests cover `git\nstatus` readability with backend-authored `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, denied Git mutation,\ncredential/sibling/arbitrary-home reads, and the\nread-only common-git carve-out.\n\n### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export\n\nThe coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.\nThe snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,\nexplicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds\n`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is\n`v1:<maximum-updated-at-UTC>:<row-count>`; an empty snapshot uses the stable sentinel\n`v1:none:0`. Migration 044 backfills `updated_at` from `created_at` and installs an update trigger.\n`policy_digest` is SHA-256 over UTF-8 canonical JSON\n(lexicographically sorted object keys, preserved rule-array order, no insignificant whitespace,\nno floats), excluding the digest field itself.\nDisabled rules are absent.\n\nOnly an enabled exact profile assignment is exportable. Unknown, disabled, or unassigned agents\nreceive a typed 404/409 response and never a global-only snapshot. Export ordering is total and\nstable: agent-profile before global, legacy priority ascending (lower number is higher priority),\ndeny before allow on ties, then\n`policy_id` ascending. Migration 044 adds constrained `destination_kind`,\n`destination_pattern`, `port`, and `updated_at` columns, parses/backfills legacy rows, and validates\nall new writes; any malformed applicable legacy row fails the whole export.\n\nSRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore\nkeeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are\nvalidated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export\nunrenderable; rules are never silently omitted. Malformed or unavailable export fails closed before\nvendor launch; it never becomes a fail-open reason or a synthetic destination list. An authored,\nsuccessfully exported empty allow set remains a valid deny-all policy. A default-allow snapshot is\nnot renderable by this backend and fails closed. The\nexport contract is authoritative for sandbox execution; the older advisory SQL matcher is not used\nto construct SRT settings. Renderer tests pin SRT 0.0.77 wildcard apex/multi-label behavior and\nprove every rendered allow is a subset of the authored effective policy. DNS names, IPv4 literals,\nand bracketed IPv6 literals are supported; CIDR belongs only to denied-resolved-address policy and\nis not accepted as a destination rule.\n\nProvider endpoints are not hard-coded in the renderer. Current seed policy lacks several vendor\nAPI domains, so dg-07 does not flip existing local lanes to `sandbox`; rollout requires an\nauthored endpoint inventory and a successful preflight. The controlled acceptance CLI exercises\nenforcement independently of production vendor endpoints.\n\nThe autopilot `local` provider is rollout-ineligible under `sandbox` until its authored hostname\nand port are exportable, its Node client is proven to use SRT's proxy path, and SRT supports the\ndestination class. Loopback, link-local, private-IP, or mDNS rejection is a fail-closed\npolicy/capability outcome, never a fail-open reason.\n\nThe renderer always supplies `deniedResolvedAddresses` for loopback, link-local, cloud metadata,\nRFC1918, CGNAT, and IPv6 ULA ranges. An explicit allow whose literal target is private is\nunrenderable and fails closed. DNS resolution into any baseline-denied range remains denied.\n\n### D5 — Sanitize boundary-shaping environment, do not claim secret brokering\n\nThe child environment is constructed from a positive allowlist rather than copied from the\ncoordinator. It contains only safe locale/terminal/time variables (`LANG`, `LC_*`, `TERM`, `TZ`),\nbackend-authored `HOME`, XDG, temporary and `PATH` variables, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, and the\nselected lane's single authored credential key. Proxy variables are set exclusively by SRT for a\nsandboxed child; the backend never injects them. Coordinator/API/database/Cloudflare variables and credentials for\nother vendors are absent. As defense in depth, the environment passed to SRT itself removes\nuppercase/lowercase `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`,\n`ALL_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY`; `NODE_OPTIONS`; `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`,\n`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`; `PYTHONPATH`, `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONSTARTUP`,\n`RUBYOPT`, `RUBYLIB`, `PERL5OPT`, `PERL5LIB`, `BASH_ENV`, and `ENV`; Git directory, worktree,\nindex, object, alternate-object, and config override variables; and `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP`.\nSRT may then author the proxy variables its child needs. This prevents an ambient parent proxy\nfrom bypassing address checks. The unsandboxed compatibility path retains the caller's original\nenvironment byte for byte. Runtime discovery records absolute Node, SRT entrypoint, `bwrap`,\n`socat`, and `rg` paths and constructs PATH from their parents, fixed root-owned non-writable\nsystem directories, and explicitly configured tool directories inside the canonical worktree;\nvendor executables are absolute and inherited descriptors are closed. Environment-backed vendor\ncredentials remain readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and the\ndownstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.\n\n### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence\n\nOnly unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe\nmay run the original command. The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,\nit appends a caller-generated stable `event_id` and fsyncs canonical JSONL under\n`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-events/outbox.jsonl`, with a 0700\nparent, 0600 file, advisory lock, and directory fsync. The state root must be absolute,\noperator-owned, no-follow/no-symlink, and outside every checkout; relative, wrong-owner,\ncheckout-contained, or symlinked roots fail closed. It is never exposed as sandbox-writable.\nFailure of both blocks dispatch. Unsafe root,\nunrenderable policy, materialization failure, and all post-SRT-start failures fail closed.\n\nEach later event attempt drains older outbox entries before writing the new one, removing a record\nonly after the endpoint acknowledges its `event_id`. Compaction holds the lock, writes a\nsame-directory 0600 temporary file, fsyncs it, atomically replaces the outbox, and fsyncs the\ndirectory. Migration 044 makes `event_id` unique; replay returns the original durable audit row id.\nThe shared `skills/shared/sandbox_audit.py` client/outbox is the frozen audit port consumed by the\nprocess backend; `skills/shared` owns both modules, `wp-policy-audit` implements the port, and\n`wp-runtime` depends on it rather than inventing a second persistence path. Coordinator evaluation backends load the shared process\nbackend through the existing explicit `SKILLS_ROOT` file-loader pattern. Audit payloads\ncontain key names and digests, never prompt/argv bodies, settings bodies, or secret values. The\ndispatch-host service principal must have coordinator trust level 3 or greater for cross-agent\nexport/audit. Rejection is reported distinctly as `authorization_failed`; if the endpoint rejects\nthe event, no audit row is claimed and the vendor process does not start.\n\nOutbox resource use is bounded: each canonical record is at most 64 KiB; the active outbox is at\nmost 10,000 records or 64 MiB; one launch drains at most 100 records or five seconds with explicit\nconnect/read deadlines and a five-second lock wait. Reaching an active-outbox bound fails closed.\nDead letters rotate at 64 MiB and are retained for 30 days. Structured counters/logs report active\nrecord count/bytes, oldest age, drain failures, permanent rejections, and dead-letter count/bytes.\n\n### D7 — Pin and probe SRT\n\nThe repository pins `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity and Node\n>=20.11.0. `install.sh` and CI may run `npm ci` in the primary checkout's\n`tools/sandbox-runtime`; dispatch performs no installation.
